description: Baselined state of the Claude Code harness gates that can flip with no local trace. Consumed by scripts/harness-gate-check.cjs, run daily by the constraint-register entry `harness-gate-drift`. Every expectation below was derived by reading ONE specific CC bundle (see cc_version + provenance), so the version pin is load-bearing rather than incidental: a new bundle invalidates the derivation even when no flag moved. Re-baseline only after re-running the unless-asked gate hunt; the check never rewrites this file.
provenance: _runs/2026-10-16/lead/cc-update-302/CC-UPDATE-302.md (re-derivation at 2.1.302 by a lead cc-update lane; the .302 ELF landed 2026-10-16 13:52 local and the launcher symlink, re-created 13:55 local, resolves to .302; the .301 ELF is still on disk and every .301 count compared here was re-read from it; baselined_at is the run-3 check time (evidence/harness-gate-check-302-run3.txt), read through the check's own reader from a lead session running 2.1.302 because the Bash secret-read guard refuses a direct cache projection: the 7 pinned flag expectations and the workflowSizeGuideline setting HOLD (8 rows) and tengu_violin_fret live true = RED by design under the standing MONITOR ruling, a single drift line with no notes; runs 1 and 2 read the cache minutes after the launcher flip while only .301 processes ran, and .301 lanes were still running at run 3, so the last cache writer is not recorded and a .302 re-fetch is not proven; the cache key count and the unmonitored keys were not measured; binary: every gate code default and gating condition re-read at .302 and unchanged (hazel default 3 with an integer >= 1 validator and env -> clientData -> GrowthBook order, fennel default false and opus_5_prompt_bundle-gated, slate default true, thistle default 'default' with the same env -> clientData -> GrowthBook -> model-floor order, heron default empty with client data read first, kairos code default true, workflows default true, violin_fret a checkGate boolean behind the same desktop consent AND chain, workflowSizeGuideline default medium with caps 5/10/50); every monitored anchor count is flat .301 -> .302; tengu inventory .301 -> .302 +24/-6 raw (3,109 -> 3,127), no added or removed key is a monitored gate or haiku-named, the violin family adds tengu_violin_colophony (code default false; one setter and two readers, all in remote and served permission routing, evidence/colophony-302.txt: when true, a computer-folder tool request whose input is not exactly three non-empty strings is denied, and a valid one is reshaped and still passed to a dialog or the host; no approval, auto-answer or mode-change path in the sites read; its cache value was not measured); help is byte-identical to .301; hook event set identical (33) with identical per-name literal counts; the haiku45 helper resolver still returns claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 to the startup quota probe, verify_api_key and rewind_limit_question, a managed deniedModels entry claude-haiku-4-5 (policy file /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json on Linux) still blocks it with dates ignored, and the fallback returns ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL first when it is set, else the ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL pin when it is not itself denied (a denied fallback goes to the main model), and a user-level value of either is not ruled out; the .301 caveat stands, not re-read at .302: a modelOverrides remap (applied to the model map before the deny check) can change that id (Codex audit finding A-01); prior baseline: _runs/2026-10-16/lead/rebaseline-301/REBASELINE-2.1.301.md)

tengu_hazel_trellis.why: subagent nesting depth cap (hunt G1/N1). A REDUCTION silently breaks lead -> orchestrator -> auditor chains mid-run with a thrown AgentPreconditionError. A raise is a note rather than a failure, but still needs the doctrine text updated (docs/cc-version-gotchas.md still claims 5). This expectation IS fold F2 -- there is no separate register entry for nesting depth.

tengu_fennel_godwit.why: kill-switch for the blanket 'do not call the AgentTool unless the user requested it' prompt section (hunt G2). false = the prohibition is ARMED and model-gated to opus_5_prompt_bundle models; true would disarm it. Monitored because this value governs whether an Opus-5-led session inherits the prohibition, and it moves server-side.

tengu_thistle_grebe.why: delegation steer (hunt G5). 'default' keeps the pro-delegation prompt text. 'no_nudges' drops it; 'counter_steer' injects text forbidding a subagent spawned to review or double-check work, which contradicts feedback_advisor-fallback (HARD: review never off) and feedback_model-trust-opus5-sonnet5 (HARD: master review over all work).

tengu_heron_brook.why: override text for the Agent-tool prohibition section (hunt G2). Absent on this rig. A non-empty string injects arbitrary vendor-supplied prompt text into every session's system prompt with no other local record.

tengu_kairos_cron_durable.why: cron durability (hunt G9/N6). false = all scheduled jobs are session-only, which is what .claude/rules/workflows.md tells sessions to assume. The persistence path (.claude/scheduled_tasks.json) is implemented and the CODE default is true, so this is one server-side flip from live.

tengu_workflows_enabled.why: presence of the Workflow tool (hunt G3). Pinned so a silent removal surfaces as drift instead of as tooling that mysteriously stopped existing.

tengu_slate_bittern.why: extra gate ANDed into the opus5_reduced_delegation prompt section: that section renders only when the model carries opus_5_prompt_bundle AND tengu_fennel_godwit is false AND this flag reads true. The bundle reads it with a code default of TRUE, and a clean rig has no cache entry, which is why the 2.1.257 and 2.1.258 derivations both NAMED this gap and could not express it -- an equals pin would have turned a legitimately absent key into a false red. Pinned absent-or-default at 2.1.259 now that the mode exists. A server-pushed false would silently DISARM the anti-delegation section: a capability change with no other local trace.

tengu_violin_fret.why: unattended-serving gate introduced at 2.1.259. VERIFIED (static read of the 2.1.259 and 2.1.260 bundles): the flag exists, is read through both a sync and an async accessor with a code default of FALSE, sits in the same minified module as the literals unattended-serving:v1:auto-arm-classifier and unattended-serving-consent.json, has a telemetry sibling recording accepted/revoked/declined next to a default-permission-mode update, and ships in the same release as --permission-prompts none. INFERENCE, NOT PROVEN: that a true value ALONE arms an auto-mode classifier for unattended serving. Other conditions are ANDed with it and no behavioural probe was run, so the coupling is read from co-location, not from execution. Baselined at the code default so that a server-pushed true reads RED. The durable cache has carried true since at least 2026-09-03T04:42Z (still true at the 2026-09-04T07:55Z cache stamp) and the owner RULED on 2026-09-03: MONITOR -- keep this expectation at false, keep the check red, never baseline the live true away. This red is the intended standing state, not a defect; only a behavioural probe of the unattended-serving path could change the expectation.

workflowSizeGuideline.why: top-level ~/.claude.json setting, not a GrowthBook flag (hunt G7/C(d)). 'medium' = the injected 'keep workflows under 10 agents' guideline (15 before 2.1.271). Pinned so a /config change or a vendor default move is visible; the bundle carries the enum ['unrestricted','small','medium','large'] with a default of 'medium' and the caps {small:5,medium:10,large:50} (medium was 15 before 2.1.271). Minified identifier names are deliberately NOT recorded -- they are renamed by the bundler between releases (2.1.258 to 2.1.259 renamed both of these) and citing them invites a phantom-drift chase.

caveat: BOUNDED, NOT ELIMINATED: tengu_heron_brook and tengu_thistle_grebe are also resolvable from per-session server-pushed client data (a client-data accessor consulted BEFORE the feature flag; the minified name is not recorded here because it is renamed between releases), which is never persisted locally. A client-data override is invisible to this baseline. The local GrowthBook cache is the only durable surface, so a green line means no DURABLE drift -- not that no override is possible.
